fields.reasoning: workflows-are-the-rules: recoveries that belong to a step stay in that step's workflow, and the watchdog only resumes runs, so the workflow's own steps (including merge) still decide. That makes it a backstop, not a second implementation of the three bug fixes, and it never merges outside a workflow. The intent says 'rebase', but bug 01M6WBVX and the repo's practice say merge origin/main, never rebase or force-push (force-push is denied here), so the watchdog merges. Owner-attended runs are left alone, as daemonNudgeStalled already does, because the owner may be the one the run waits on. The 20m nudge reuses today's daemonNudgeText threshold; doubling it before a retry gives the session one chance to answer. Budget 2 and one CI rerun match the intent's 'rerun failed CI once' and the bug requests' 'retry once', with one spare for a stall. warn-dont-safeguard: everything is policy with defaults in rhiza.toml, and it warns (inbox, log, health) rather than blocking.
fields.statement: (1) The watchdog is the daemon-level backstop; the three bug requests stay separate and ship on their own. Each adds a first-line recovery inside its workflow step (a step retries once on a vanished go $WORK, plan reruns failed CI once, ship-change merges main on a conflict). The watchdog acts only on what those miss: a run that has stalled, or has ended on a known transient signature. It never duplicates a step's recovery while the step is still live. Its resume counts against its own per-run retry budget, separate from any step's. (2) Stalled step (no journal entry or session report past its limit), autonomous runs only: first nudge the session (today's daemonNudge). If there is still no progress after a second limit, stop the step and run resume --retry, logging one line and charging the run's budget. Once the budget is spent, leave an inbox item naming what was tried. Owner-attended runs get only the log line and an inbox item, never a stop or retry. (3) A PR with no CI because it conflicts with main: the watchdog merges origin/main into the branch and pushes normally (never rebase or force-push), then records the push in the run's ship state. If the merge conflicts, it resumes the run so the run's own conflict handling (the 01M6WBVX fixer, once shipped) takes it; until then it leaves an inbox item. A green PR its run never merged: the watchdog resumes the run with --retry so the workflow's own merge step merges it, and never merges outside a workflow. If that workflow's merge needs the owner, it leaves an inbox item instead. Every recovery caused by a bug files one deduplicated bug request with the evidence. (4) Shipped defaults, under [rhiza.daemon.watchdog] in rhiza.toml, all overridable per repo and per workflow step kind: enabled = true; nudge after 20m idle for agent steps (as today), then retry after 40m; command steps 30m; CI and PR wait steps 90m; retry budget 2 per run; failed CI rerun once per PR head; poll-behind warning when a poll takes over 3x the poll interval; file_bugs = true; act only on autonomous runs.
